cinematic_inference.protagonist_occupation: Conservation Technician at a Small Regional Museum
cinematic_inference.body_design: 49–51-year-old woman, 5'5", medium build with a compact, sturdy frame and soft musculature; hands with visible veins and faint calluses from careful manual work; posture slightly forward-leaning when at a bench, relaxed when off duty.
cinematic_inference.ethnicity_design: Midwestern White (Northern European ancestry), freckle-sprinkled skin with light age spots.
cinematic_inference.hair_design: Salt-and-pepper shoulder-length bob, usually pulled back into a low clip or loose knot in the lab; a few wisps left free around the face for a quietly worn look.
cinematic_inference.wardrobe_design: Casual-conservative everyday mix: well-fitting neutral cardigans and tailored chambray shirts, soft wool trousers and practical ankle boots or brown leather loafers; a single tasteful vintage silk scarf and a modest brooch for slightly dressier occasions; a sturdy chore-style cotton coat for field installs and a simple apron or lab smock for conservation work.
cinematic_inference.casting_rationale: The chosen physical and wardrobe details create a visually specific, lived-in character who reads as methodical and steady on camera; the salt-and-pepper hair and modest vintage accent signal quiet personal history without distractingly theatrical choices. The compact, robust body and hand detail emphasize tactile, hands-on conservation work and produce strong, cinematic close-ups for treatment scenes while fitting the modest economic and cultural tone.

director_profile.social_dynamics: Mostly solitary at work, she collaborates in small teams with a curator, registrar, and a rotating set of volunteers or student interns; polite and reserved with donors and board members, capable of guarded warmth with trusted colleagues and one or two community members.
director_profile.professional_vibe: Conscientious, precise, deliberate — she treats objects with quiet reverence, prefers routines, keeps meticulous notes and labels, and moves at a steady unhurried pace even under stress.
director_profile.visual_vibe: Soft, natural light, close-ups of hands and tools, tidy benches and archival boxes, muted earthy palette (beiges, denim blue, slate gray) with one or two warm accents (vintage silk scarf, wooden tool handles); textural detail (frayed textile fibers, vellum, metal clasps) and moderate contrasts between clean conservation lab and dim storage vaults.

director_profile.parallel_story_rule: Do not transform the museum into a religious or family institution; any churchgoing or family scenes belong exclusively to off-duty life and must remain separate from the conservation workplace.

occupation_selection.job_title: Conservation Technician at a Small Regional Museum
occupation_selection.rationale: This role balances a quiet, meticulous temperament with rich, cinematic visuals and varied work settings—conservation labs, gallery prep, storage vaults, and community exhibit installs—without relying on meetings or bureaucratic drama. It fits her methodical, precise work style and modest economic independence (small regional museums pay modestly but steadily), allows mostly solitary, hands‑on activity punctuated by small-team interactions with curators, registrars, and occasional donors or volunteers, and supports a conservative-casual wardrobe with one or two tasteful vintage pieces. Storywise it offers active sequences (treatment of fragile textiles/papers, delicate sewing/repair, condition reporting, mounting pieces for display, and supervising handling during installations) plus emotional beats when objects trigger memory or conflict—good material for a visually engaging, character-driven film.
